name: Martin Pfister
bio: Martin Pfister (born 31 July 1963 in Zug) is a Swiss historian, former teacher and politician of The Centre (Die Mitte) who has served as a member of the Swiss Federal Council since April 2025, heading the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (VBS/DDPS). He grew up in Zug and Allenwinden, where he resides with his family, and holds citizenship of Waldkirch (SG). Trained as a primary teacher at the St Michael Teacher Training College and a master's graduate in history and German from the University of Fribourg, he worked as a teacher, academic assistant and later in association management and non-profit consulting before entering full-time politics. He is also an Oberst (Colonel) in the Swiss Army with a background in disaster-relief units. Pfister began his political career in the municipality of Baar, was elected to the Cantonal Council (Kantonsrat) of Zug in 2006, and served as a member of the Zug Executive Council (Regierungsrat) and head of its Health Department from 2016 to 2025, including as Landammann (cantonal president) in 2021/2022. As Zug's health director he played a prominent role in the cantonal COVID-19 response. In March 2025 the Federal Assembly elected him to the Federal Council to succeed Viola Amherd, having been widely seen as an outsider against the favourite Markus Ritter. He took office on 1 April 2025 as head of the defence department.
